obligation: Customs broker breach notice to CBP
trigger: Any known breach of electronic or physical records relating to the broker's customs business (for example a mailbox or archive holding client entries, invoices, or Form 5106 data read or copied by an attacker). Clock starts at discovery of the breach
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery, electronically, including any known compromised importer identification numbers
notify: CBP Office of Information Technology Security Operations Center (cbpsoc@cbp.dhs.gov); questions by phone at the number posted on CBP.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - licensed customs broker

obligation: Customs broker breach notice follow-up
trigger: After the initial 72-hour notice
deadline: Updated list of additional compromised importer identification numbers within 10 business days of the notice; any later information within 72 hours of discovering it
notify: CBP Security Operations Center (electronically)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - licensed customs broker

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access of electronic data) involving personal information of Florida residents: Social Security numbers of individual importers or employees; financial account numbers with access codes; an email address with a password that permits access to an online account. Clock starts at determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination; 15 more days only if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - plan to the 30-day date

obligation: Florida notice not required determination
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only with counsel's advice

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension in 501.171(3)(a) applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the company holds Social Security numbers for about 25 individual importers and 7 employees

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely at this size

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay on the agency's written request for the period it specifies
notify: Hold Florida individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (inbound; MSP, SaaS, and backup vendors)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a third-party agent that stores or processes personal information for the company
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent's determination
notify: The company (Office and Compliance Manager); the company then sends the notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - add to the MSP and backup contracts

obligation: Other states' breach laws
trigger: Affected individual importers or employees who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected individuals

obligation: Client notice under client terms
citation: Client terms of service and CTPAT business partner commitments (contract)
trigger: Exposure of a client's records or a payment made on the client's behalf going astray
deadline: Per contract; the company commits to notify affected clients within 72 hours, matching the CBP clock
notify: Affected clients; CTPAT importer clients' security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal; N48-49-R05 questionnaires ask for it

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Wire fraud report to the bank and the FBI
citation: Bank account agreement (contract); voluntary report to the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3)
trigger: A wire sent on fraudulent instructions
deadline: Immediately: the bank's fraud line first for a recall request; IC3 complaint the same day
notify: Company's bank fraud line; IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual and voluntary, not a legal deadline

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident, funds transfer fraud, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics; the social engineering sublimit requires the call-back procedure to have been followed
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: USCG maritime cyber incident report
trigger: Actual or threatened cyber incident involving or endangering any vessel, harbor, port, or waterfront facility
deadline: Immediately
notify: FBI, CISA, and the Captain of the Port; National Response Center for reportable cyber incidents
applies_at_this_tier: No - an office BEC does not involve or endanger a vessel or waterfront facility. Recheck if an incident affects a terminal or carrier system the company can reach

obligation: TSA SD cybersecurity incident reporting (rail, passenger rail and transit, pipeline)
trigger: Cybersecurity incident at a designated operator
deadline: No later than 72 hours after identification (SD Sec. II.C; verified for SD 1580-21-01E and SD Pipeline-2021-01G 2026-10-05); supplemental information within 24 hours of it becoming available
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a TSA-designated operator

obligation: Aviation significant cybersecurity incident reporting
citation: TSA airport and aircraft operator security programs (SSI) (N48-49-R04)
trigger: Significant cybersecurity incident at a regulated airport or aircraft operator
deadline: Per security program (SSI; timeline not publicly verified)
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - not an airport or aircraft operator; no air cargo

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Registrant determines an incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: No - privately held

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (voluntary until then); proposed criteria target entities above the SBA size standard or meeting sector criteria. Recheck when final

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
trigger: Contractor identifies a Kaspersky covered article
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further report within 10 business days
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts
